setup.text: [someone claiming to be your daughter says she dropped her phone in water and this is a borrowed number]

ask.text: [she says she cannot get into her banking and needs a bill paid in the next hour]
[she gives a stranger's account to transfer to and asks you not to call, since the borrowed phone cannot take calls]

usualEnding: The transfer reaches a stranger and the borrowed number stops answering. Your daughter still has her phone.
neverAsks: A real relative can take a call on the number you already have, and never asks you to keep a money request secret.

parts.text: Pa, I landed. The taxi queue is long.
Can you check if I left my charger on the kitchen table?
Will call once I am home.

setup.text: [a recruiter offers flexible work liking videos and rating hotels, paid daily]

ask.text: [after two small payouts, the next set of tasks needs a top-up to unlock a bigger commission]
[a link to a private task group]

usualEnding: The two small payouts are real. The top-up is not returned, and the next task needs a bigger one.
neverAsks: A real employer never asks you to pay a top-up to get paid.

parts.text: Thanks for applying for the weekend retail role.
Can you come for a short interview on Thursday at 2 pm at the store?
Reply with a yes or suggest another day.

setup.text: [a mentor adds you to a group where members post screenshots of daily gains]
[the mentor shares a professional-looking profile and a licence number to look up]

ask.text: [a limited slot in this week's trade closes tonight; the first deposit is small]
[the deposit goes to a personal account, not a brokerage]

usualEnding: The dashboard shows gains that cannot be withdrawn without a fee. The fee is paid, and the group vanishes.
neverAsks: A licensed adviser never promises fixed returns, never recruits through a private group and never asks for a fee to withdraw.

parts.text: The personal finance talk at the community centre is this Saturday, 10 am.
It is free and run by the national financial education programme.
I signed us both up. No payment, just bring a notebook.
Want to have breakfast before?

ask.text: [a text says a parcel in your name held suspicious items and a case has been opened by the police]
[it says you must call back within two hours and keep the matter confidential while the investigation runs]

usualEnding: The call back leads to an officer who asks you to move your savings to a safe account. The account is theirs.
neverAsks: The police never ask for money, bank details or a code by message or call, and never tell you to keep an investigation secret.

parts.text: Your neighbourhood police post is holding a scam awareness talk on Sunday at 10 am.
Reply to reserve a seat for you and a family member.

ask.text: [a courier text says a parcel could not be delivered because the address is incomplete]
[a link to update the address and pay a small redelivery fee before the parcel is returned tonight]

usualEnding: The page takes the card details for the small fee. A much larger charge follows.
neverAsks: A courier never asks for a fee through a link in a message to release or redeliver a parcel.

parts.text: Your parcel will arrive today between 2 and 6 pm.
Reply 1 to leave it at the door or 2 to hand it over in person.

setup.text: [a message styled as your bank says unusual activity was found on your account]

ask.text: [it says the account will be suspended in 30 minutes unless you confirm your identity]
[a link to a page that asks for your login and the one-time code sent to your phone]

usualEnding: The login and the code let someone log in as you. The account is emptied before the bank opens.
neverAsks: A bank never asks for a login, PIN or one-time code through a link in a message.

parts.text: A card payment of 86.40 at a supermarket was approved at 6:12 pm.
Your updated balance is in the app.
If this was not you, call the number on the back of your card.

setup.text: [a message from someone using your manager's name says they are in a meeting and cannot talk]

ask.text: [they ask you to pay a supplier invoice today to a new bank account because the old one is under audit]
[they ask you to handle it quietly and confirm when done]

usualEnding: The invoice is paid to the new account. The real supplier chases the unpaid invoice a week later.
neverAsks: A real manager or supplier never changes a bank account by message alone, and can confirm on the number you already have.

parts.text: Hi, the client moved the demo to 3 pm tomorrow.
Can you book the small meeting room and send the invite?
Call me if the room is taken.
